authorization.rationale: The Collection-1 restriction accepted on 2026-09-05 cannot satisfy the accepted extent-coverage contract in the wet season, and no configuration reachable under the previous single-policy contract can. A distinct, explicitly declared wet-season source regime is accepted instead of lowering the coverage floor or widening the registry for the whole year.

rejected_alternatives.option: relax the scene cloud filter alone
rejected_alternatives.measured: January reaches 0.8314 even with the filter removed entirely
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: does not clear the floor in any wet-season month
ESA has barely reprocessed the wet season of 2016-2022 onto the Collection-1 lineage, so the years carry almost no admissible data

rejected_alternatives.measured: clears the floor, but 65% of the January baseline would come from the two strong El Nino years
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: drought years would define the wet-season normal, biasing the detector toward under-detection of loss

rejected_alternatives.option: widen the reviewed registry for the whole year
rejected_alternatives.measured: clears the floor but leaves 59.3% of January below three contributions
rejected_alternatives.rejected_because: imports the reproducibility risk into the eight months that do not need it, and does not solve contribution depth
Package 2A.2 discipline exists to prevent a baseline that validates while being unusable; the accepted policy clears the floor, so it is not relaxed

regimes.reproducibility_note: every admitted product is on the Collection-1 lineage and is not subject to further ESA reprocessing

admits pre-Collection-1 products that ESA has not yet reprocessed and is actively reprocessing; this regime is expected to be retired and the wet season rebuilt on the Collection-1 lineage once that reprocessing reaches these months
regimes.retirement_condition: the wet-season months of the accepted source years are fully available on the Collection-1 lineage

cloud_filter_basis.why_not_looser: A cloud-leakage test found no systematic contamination in NDMI or NBR - the sign was inconsistent and reversed in March - but EVI2, the only index using the red band that thin cloud brightens most, carries a positive offset that grows monotonically with cloud: +0.027 at 40-60% and +0.043 at 60-80%, against a clean January dispersion of 0.087. The 60 bound takes the coverage while holding that one measured bias at its smaller value.
cloud_filter_basis.test_limits: the comparison covered 12-25% of the extent in January and 74.5% in March, spanned two months, and did not fully separate contamination from the correlation between cloud and rainfall; it is not a general clearance

science_bindings_unchanged.statistics: monthly median and population standard deviation over datatake composites
